title: Senior Security Engineer (m/f/d)
description:
Your mission Do you want to do more than just write security concepts - and put your decisions into practice directly? Do you see cloud security not as a compliance checklist, but as the combination of threat modeling, Infrastructure as Code, and genuine hands-on engineering? Then we are looking for you to join our CISO team as a Senior Security Engineer (m/f/d) in a hybrid working model in Munich, Berlin or Halle (Saale) .
You will join a three-person team where responsibility is genuinely shared: no ticket queues and no “that’s not my area.” We plan together, cover for one another, and usually implement and operate the security controls we design ourselves. This means you will see the impact of your work immediately - not at some point in the distant future.
Your Responsibilities - Security Architecture & Cloud Guardrails: You will take technical ownership of the security architecture and controls across our Azure environment - from Defender for Cloud and Microsoft Sentinel to Log Analytics. You will build and maintain the corresponding guardrails directly in Terraform.
- Detection Engineering: You will develop and continuously improve our detections in close collaboration with our Security Analyst, who is responsible for day-to-day SIEM monitoring and triage. You will work as a well-coordinated team rather than in separate silos.
- Vulnerability Management: You will further develop our vulnerability management and monitoring across a hybrid environment. This includes our growing cloud landscape as well as the existing on-premises stack for as long as the migration is ongoing.
- Security Beyond the Cloud: You will contribute your expertise beyond cloud security, including identity, endpoint security, application security, incident response, and AI. Using your security engineering skills, you will, for example, develop tooling for AI-assisted penetration testing within our team and translate it into practical, scalable processes.
- AI-Assisted Engineering: You will use tools such as Claude Code to build and maintain internal security tools and automations. At the same time, you will help us identify AI-specific risks early—from the secure use of AI coding assistants to prompt injection.

Your skillset - Azure Security & Certifications: You have at least five years of experience in security engineering and several years of hands-on experience implementing Azure security. You hold an AZ-500 certification or have equivalent practical expertise. SC-100, CISSP, CCSP, or Security+ certifications are a plus.
- Infrastructure & Automation: You can confidently read, write, and further develop security-related Terraform code. Experience with Python, Django, PowerShell, or AI-assisted development is a plus.
- Identity & Detection: You have practical experience with Entra ID, RBAC, and PIM, as well as solid knowledge of network security, SIEM, and detection engineering.
- Offensive Security & Vulnerability Management: Ideally, you have experience with traditional or AI-assisted penetration testing and with tools such as Tenable or Microsoft Defender Vulnerability Management.
- Hands-On Mindset: You do not just design security controls -you implement and operate them in practice. When you identify a problem, you do not wait for a ticket; you take ownership and develop a solution.
- Collaboration & Communication: You share knowledge and responsibility and work closely with the team on areas of joint ownership. You communicate confidently and professionally in English. German is a plus, but not a requirement.
Experience with an ongoing cloud migration and AI/LLM security is welcome, but not essential. What matters to us is what you can genuinely do - substance beats buzzword bingo. 

Your winning deal - Your benefits : In addition to 30 days of vacation , we also offer you a job lunch allowance (€69 per month), a “ Givve ” card (topped up with €50 per month) or a subsidized membership with Wellpass, discounts via “ Corporate Benefits” , the option of leasing a JobRad , pension contributions (occupational pension & VL) and great team and company events .
- Your workplace : Y ou will work in a flexible, hybrid model from one of our dog-friendly and modern offices and will have the opportunity to do “ work from abroad ” within the EU for 2 weeks a year (* only applies to employees with an EU passport ) 
- Your footprint: A position in a profitable company where you have the freedom and confidence to help shape it and work with us on the “ future of work ” . 
- The values : We score highly with an open, authentic culture and a high- performing and humorous team that is already looking forward to making bold decisions with you and breaking new ground that will lead us to sustainable success . 
- Your opportunity : From day one , you will have the opportunity to take on responsibility , drive innovation and develop the company and yourself together with a team of experts.

title: Senior Software Engineer (Trust)
description:
Beneath a simple yet elegant user interface lies a complex system of functionalities. Our AI-powered product uses advanced image recognition, facial verification, face recognition, facial anti-spoofing (liveness detection), and behavior analysis to make identity decisions. We help our partners build onboarding processes that ensure good people get things done and bad folks get stopped.

But knowing who someone is only gets you halfway. The next question is whether they can be trusted — and answering it means checking a person's identity data against the authoritative sources that hold the truth. Every country does this differently: a different registry, a different database, a different set of rules about what can be checked and how.

To take our platform to the next level, we're looking for a Senior Software Engineer to join the Trust team. This team builds and operates the services that validate a person's identity data against country-specific authoritative sources — government registries, national databases, AML and sanctions screening — and turns that patchwork of very different upstreams into a single, dependable trust signal our customers can act on. Alongside sibling teams like Trust Registries and Trusted Documents, your work directly determines how many countries we can cover, how fast we can launch a new one, and how much our partners can rely on the answer we give them.

YOU'LL HELP US PROTECT HONEST PEOPLE ONLINE BY: 

- Designing, building, and operating Trust's backend services — the integrations with external identity data sources and the validation logic on top of them — with a strong focus on reliability, scalability, and maintainability

- Expanding our global coverage: onboarding new countries and data sources quickly, and building the abstractions that make the next integration cheaper than the last one instead of more expensive

- Modelling messy, inconsistent upstream data into consistent, well-defined verification results — including the matching and validation rules that decide whether the data actually belongs to the person in front of us

- Making our systems resilient to upstreams we don't control — timeouts, retries and idempotency, backpressure, circuit breaking, graceful degradation, backwards-compatibility testing, SPOF elimination, and end-to-end monitoring of every provider we depend on

- Handling sensitive personal data responsibly, with regional data residency and compliance requirements designed in from the start

- Participating in on-call rotations, incident response, and postmortems to ensure our most critical checks stay healthy

- Driving engineering quality through code reviews, CI practices, runbook documentation, and mentoring teammates

YOU ARE THE RIGHT FUTURE VERIFFIAN FOR THE JOB IF YOU HAVE: 

- 5+ years of experience building large-scale backend applications with Python, including event-driven and async architectures with message queues (e.g. SQS, RabbitMQ, or similar)

- Hands-on experience integrating with third-party APIs at scale — and a healthy respect for what happens when they're slow, flaky, undocumented, or quietly change their response format

- Proven ownership of production-critical services — you understand what it means to be on-call and take reliability seriously

- Deep experience designing for resilience in distributed systems: idempotency, retries, backpressure, timeouts, backwards compatibility

- Strong data modelling instincts — you can turn heterogeneous, inconsistent external data into a clean domain model that holds up as the number of sources grows

title: CENTRALE LYON - Postdoctoral Researcher Position Deep Learning for Functional-Oxide Growth Video-to-Spectrum Prediction by RHEED / XRD Fusion
description:
PROJECT OVERVIEW 

We are looking for a highly motivated Postdoctoral Researcher to develop innovative deeplearning models that predict the structure of functional-oxide thin films directly from their growth dynamics. Positioned at the interface between Artificial Intelligence and materials physics, the OXYD-IA project aims to design a deep model able to predict the final X-ray Diffraction (XRD) spectrum of an oxide thin film from the sole Reflection High-Energy Electron Diffraction (RHEED) video recorded during its growth by Molecular Beam Epitaxy (MBE). 

The resulting tool will open the way to predictive, in situ control of oxide epitaxy – a process today dominated by a costly trial-and-error approach, in which the structural and functional properties of the films are only validated ex situ. You will join a genuinely multidisciplinary collaboration between the INL (Institut des Nanotechnologies de Lyon), which provides the operando experimental data and materials-physics expertise, and the LIRIS (équipe Imagine), which provides the deep video-learning and probabilistic-modelling methodology – both at École Centrale de Lyon. 

A high-impact opportunity. AI for experimental physics is a fast-growing field, and OXYD-IA offers a genuine first-mover advantage within it: you would work on a unique, unpublished dataset of paired RHEED videos and XRD spectra to build one of the first video-to-spectrum models with calibrated uncertainty for oxide growth. By learning directly from experimental 1 data, such a model can short-circuit the traditional trial-and-error loop, accelerate discovery and drastically cut experimental time, cost, precursor consumption and instrument occupancy – turning routine in situ diagnostics into predictive tools. 

Scientific context. Epitaxial perovskite-oxide thin films exhibit rich, tunable functional properties (thermoelectricity, ferroelectricity, piezoelectricity) governed by their structure and composition, themselves correlated with the growth conditions. MBE offers independent control of each element but, applied to oxides, is notoriously unstable and poorly reproducible because of the oxidising atmosphere. RHEED tracks the surface dynamics in real time (lattice parameter, surface reconstructions, roughness) but does not give access to the final bulk microstructure, which is only reachable ex situ via XRD / XRR. There is therefore a strong physical link – so far unexploited quantitatively – between RHEED dynamics and final XRD microstructure, which OXYD-IA proposes to learn directly.

Figure 1 – OXYD-IA pipeline. At inference, the RHEED video acquired during growth (INL) feeds a deep video encoder (LIRIS) and a probabilistic regression module that predicts the final XRD spectrum together with its uncertainty. During training, the predicted spectrum is compared with the ex situ XRD / XRR spectrum measured at INL (ground truth); this discrepancy is the supervised learning signal that adjusts the model parameters.

KEY RESEARCH AREAS AND RESPONSIBILITIES 

You will drive the core computational research along a risk-managed, phased 12-month roadmap. The primary target is a versioned RHEED / XRD dataset, growth-regime classification and probabilistic regression of the key structural parameters with calibrated uncertainty; full-spectrum prediction, a real-time demonstrator and cross-oxide generalisation are stretch and follow-on objectives. The work is organised around three technical pillars: 

1. Corpus structuring and spatio-temporal RHEED representation • Build a versioned dataset by cleaning, temporally aligning and pairing the RHEED video sequences, the associated MBE parameters (temperature, oxygen pressure, source fluxes) and the ex situ XRD / XRR spectra (SrTiO3 reference system). • Pre-train, in a self-supervised manner, a spatio-temporal video encoder (3D CNN, e.g. R(2+1)D, or temporal Vision Transformer) fine-tuned on the laboratory corpus. • Perform fuzzy / Bayesian classification of the growth regimes (2D vs. 3D modes, transitions, RHEED oscillations), building on LIRIS expertise in the statistical analysis of sequences. 

2. Probabilistic RHEED →XRD regression with uncertainty quantification • Design a latent representation that couples the video encoding with the physical MBE parameters. • Learn stepwise – first scalar structural parameters (lattice parameter, density, mosaicity), more robust at small N, then the full 1D XRD spectrum. • Provide calibrated uncertainty estimates (Bayesian approaches or deep ensembles), indispensable for guiding real-time decisions during growth. 

3. Real-time demonstrator and dissemination (stretch / follow-on) • Validate the model on new SrTiO3 growths and prototype an in-growth inference tool at the end of the NANOFUTUR MBE line. • Mitigate the small-data and generalisation challenges through temporal data augmentation, transfer learning from pre-trained video encoders and domain adaptation towards other functional oxides. • Contribute toward a high-impact joint publication at the AI / materials interface (the project milestone is the submission of a joint paper).

REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS 

• A Ph.D. in the field of Artificial Intelligence – Computer Science, Machine Learning, Computer Vision or Signal Processing, and we are looking for a senior postdoc with 2–5 years of post-PhD experience. 

• Deep learning on sequential / video data: demonstrable, hands-on experience with 3D CNNs, temporal transformers and / or probabilistic models. Proficiency in Python and PyTorch (or TensorFlow) is mandatory. 

• A genuine appetite for physics: a strong curiosity for, or prior exposure to, experimental physics and materials science. The ideal candidate carried out an AI-focused Ph.D. and is eager to apply it to a real materials-physics problem. 

• Research mindset: a track record of innovation and the ability to work autonomously on a complex, multidisciplinary project. • Software skills: experience with Git version control and reproducible research. 

• Excellent communication and scientific-writing skills in English. 

ADDITIONAL SKILLS AND COMPETENCIES 

• Self-supervised video pre-training, uncertainty quantification (Bayesian / ensembles), fuzzy classification, or domain adaptation. 

• Experience with small-sample / transfer-learning settings and handling large-scale experimental datasets.

HOW TO APPLY 

Please prepare a single PDF file containing: 

1. A detailed Curriculum Vitae, including a list of publications. 

2. A 1-page motivation letter explaining your specific interest in this project and how your background addresses the key responsibilities and qualifications listed above. 

3. The names and contact information of at least two academic references.

title: Analyst, Data Operations & Analytics (all genders)
description:
Hi there! Thanks for stopping by 👋 

Are you actively looking for a new opportunity? Or just checking the market? Well… you might just be in the right place! 

We're looking for a savvy Analyst, Data Operations & Analytics to join our Data Office in Berlin and serve as the ultimate bridge between data, product, and business teams across our Hospitality vertical. You'll turn complex business questions into clear insights, reusable data models, and reporting that help teams understand their customers and business, make better decisions, and improve operational performance. If you're ready to combine strong analytical judgment, product and business understanding, and technical expertise to elevate data standards, and make a lasting impact, this is the opportunity for you!

Lightspeed empowers the businesses at the heart of our communities, from standout retailers to unforgettable restaurants to renowned golf courses. We are a global team who fuel ambitions with technology and insight.

From online and in-person operations to multichannel sales, payments, inventory management and data-driven insights, Lightspeed helps businesses grow, deliver exceptional customer experiences and run smarter across all channels and locations.

Join our driven, diverse and inclusive team to find your people, accelerate your career and create tangible solutions that help local businesses thrive.

What you’ll be doing: 

- Build a solid understanding of Hospitality's business processes, customers, and data so you can answer questions accurately and with the right context.

- Perform analyses such as segmentation, customer health checks, and impact measurement to help teams understand how the business is performing.

- Write SQL queries and build datasets to answer stakeholder questions, pulling from multiple data sources as needed.

- Build and maintain dashboards and reports that make it easy for business partners to track KPIs and spot trends.

- Work with stakeholders to understand what they're really asking, turning loosely defined questions into a clear analysis plan, with support from senior colleagues on trickier requests.

- Present findings clearly, with visualizations and a short narrative that explains what the data shows and why it matters.

- Help spot and investigate data quality issues, documenting what you find and flagging root causes to the right people.

And a lttle bit of: 

- Stay up to date with developments, innovations, and trends in data, including state-of-the-art machine learning models and large language models (LLMs).

- Contributing as part of the wider team to achieve organisational objectives even if this means doing things that aren’t strictly within the scope of your role.

What you need to bring: 

- 2–3+ years of experience as a Data Analyst or in a similar analytics role.

- Solid SQL skills, comfortable querying and joining data across multiple sources.

- Experience with Python for data analysis is a plus.

- Experience building dashboards or reports using Looker or a similar BI tool.

- Exposure to Hospitality, Finance, Accounting, Revenue Operations, Sales, or another operational business environment is a plus.

- Comfortable turning a business question into an analysis plan, and asking clarifying questions when the ask isn't fully defined.

- Careful with data accuracy, with a good eye for spotting things that look off.

- Strong verbal and written communication skills, able to explain findings clearly to non-technical stakeholders.

- Curious, organized, and a self-starter, comfortable in a fast-paced environment.

- Familiarity with GCP, BigQuery, Dataform, GitHub, or Salesforce is a plus.

- Familiarity with Segment, Heap type of tools

We know that people are more than what’s on their CV. If you’re unsure that you have the right profile for the role... hit the ‘Apply’ button and give it a try!

What’s in it for you: 

Come live the Lightspeed experience...

- Genuine career opportunities in a company that’s creating new jobs every day

- Opportunity to make a difference; help merchants grow their businesses and become more successful by creating or improving products and addressing customer feedback

- Work in a team big enough for growth but lean enough to make a real impact

- Development of very high traffic products, used at a global scale

- Opportunities to learn and expand your skill set

- Become a valued part of the diverse and inclusive Lightspeed culture

… and enjoy a range of benefits that’ll keep you happy, healthy and (not) hungry:

- Lightspeed equity scheme (we are all owners)

- Monthly office lunch

- Work from anywhere in the world for 60 days a year

- Health and wellness benefit of 400 Euros per year

- Mental health online platform and counseling & coaching services

- Volunteer day

To all recruitment agencies: Lightspeed does not accept unsolicited agency resumes. If we have not directly engaged your company in writing to supply candidates for a specific vacancy, Lightspeed will not be responsible for any fees related to unsolicited resumes. 

Lightspeed is a proud equal opportunity employer and we are committed to creating an inclusive and barrier-free workplace. Lightspeed welcomes and encourages applications from people with disabilities. Accommodations are available on request for candidates taking part in all aspects of the selection process. 

Where to from here? 

Obviously, this has to be mutually beneficial: we want you to step into a role you love, and we want to offer you a place you’re proud to come to every day. For a glimpse into our world check out our career page here .

Lightspeed is building communities through commerce, and we need people from all backgrounds and lived experiences to do that. We were founded in 2005, in Montreal’s gay village and our original members were all part of the LGBTQ+ community. description:
About the role 

Our Security team protects Swile's products, data and engineering platform. We work with a simple principle: when something is recurring, we automate it, and when a security requirement can become code, we write the code.

As a Security Engineer Intern, you will not shadow the team, you will be part of it. You will handle real alerts, run your own audits and own projects end to end, with a dedicated mentor in the team throughout your internship.

What you will do 

Detection and response 

- Handle day to day security alerts: triage, investigate, qualify, escalate when needed.

- Improve what we detect: reduce noise, close detection gaps, propose new signals.

- Automate the recurring: when an alert or a manual check keeps coming back, script it away. This is where we expect you to leave a mark.

Security audits 

- Run targeted audits, from a few days to a few weeks, on applications, configurations or third party providers.

- Turn findings into a prioritised remediation plan rather than a list of tickets.

Projects you will own 

- Ad hoc security projects across the engineering platform.

- Security review and hardening of the tools and integrations we rely on (Dust, third party providers, internal integrations).

Fraud 

- Support fraud investigations: dig, follow the trail, understand how an abuse pattern works and how we could detect it earlier.

What we are looking for 

This is an internship, so how you think matters more than what you already know.

- You learn fast and you are genuinely curious about security.

- You are a doer: you answer quickly, you close loops, you do not let things sit.

- You are pragmatic: you calibrate your response to the actual level of urgency and risk, and you know that not everything is a P1.

- You are open minded and comfortable asking questions across engineering teams.

- You are comfortable working in English, written and spoken.

- You have some scripting ability (Python or equivalent) and a basic understanding of web applications, APIs and cloud environments.

Nice to have that would make you stand out 

- Personal projects, CTFs, homelab, bug bounty or security writeups.

- First exposure to a SIEM, to detection rules or to log analysis at scale.

- Curiosity for fraud and abuse patterns in a financial product.

What this internship is not 

- Not a pure GRC, compliance or policy writing internship.

- Not a pentest internship.

- Not a role where you watch dashboards without changing them.

Practical details 

- Location: Paris preferred.

- Duration and start date: 3-6 months internship, ASAP or from January 2027

- Mentor: a Security Engineer from the team.

title: Application Engineer (f/m/d)
description:
About TACTILIA 

At TACTILIA, we are building the industry-ready robotic hand that closes one of the biggest gaps in Physical AI. Spun out of SCHUNK, the global market leader in gripping technology, we combine a decade of robotic-hand expertise and real industrial access with the speed and ambition of a deep-tech startup.

This isn't a research project waiting for its first customer. We already have a product, customers are ready to use it, and we are launching now. Your work will directly shape the electronics, actuators, and embedded systems that make that possible.

You will join at the moment when the hard engineering questions become real product decisions: how do we make a highly capable robotic hand reliable, manufacturable, serviceable, and simple enough to deploy on a real shop floor?

The Role 

You are the bridge between a customer use case and our product. You take a task described on the shop floor, turn it into a working robot application, and translate what you learn back into concrete product requirements.

You work on humanoid and industrial platforms, in our lab and at customer sites. You are close to the hardware, responsible for making applications work in practice, and know whether a grasp still holds after ten thousand cycles.

You report to the CTO and work closely with Product, Software and Electronics.

What you will do: 

- Use case to requirement. Analyse customer applications on site, understand their technical and operational constraints, and derive specific, testable product requirements.

- Skill implementation. Implement and optimise grasping and manipulation skills on real hardware — including parameterisation, grasp strategies, task sequences and error recovery.

- Testing. Design and run application-level tests covering endurance, cycle testing, grasp success rates, robustness to object and position variance, and reproducibility.

- High-level control & integration. Integrate our hands into humanoid and industrial robots, including mechanical and electrical interfacing, commissioning, task-level programming and sequencing.

- Teleoperation & robot learning. Set up and operate teleoperation systems, record high-quality demonstrations for imitation learning, and support reinforcement-learning workflows including sim-to-real validation.

- Demo setups & showcases. Build reliable demonstrators for trade fairs, customer visits and pilot projects that can run repeatedly under real-world conditions.

- Shop floor deployment. Take applications from the lab into production environments, addressing cycle times, safety, system interfaces and integration with existing automation.

- Feedback into development. Capture field findings, failure modes and product limitations and work with Product and Engineering to translate them into concrete improvements.

- Documentation & enablement. Document applications, integration procedures and test results, and support customers and partners during deployment.

What you bring: 

- Degree in mechatronics, robotics, automation, mechanical or electrical engineering, or a comparable qualification.

- 3–8 years of experience in robot applications, commissioning, systems integration or automation engineering.

- Practical experience programming and commissioning industrial robots or cobots, with the confidence to work on live robotic cells.

- Strong Python skills; C++ is an advantage.

- Experience with ROS 2 and simulation environments such as Isaac Sim, Gazebo, MuJoCo or comparable platforms.

- Structured approach to testing — you design tests that produce measurable, reproducible results.

- Hands-on mentality — you are comfortable building fixtures, wiring systems, commissioning hardware and running tests yourself.

- Willingness to travel to customer sites and trade fairs, approximately 20–30%.

- Fluent in English and German.

Bonus: 

- Experience with grasping technology, end-of-arm tooling or dexterous manipulation.

- Experience with teleoperation systems, motion capture or VR-based robot control.

- Practical experience with imitation learning, behaviour cloning or reinforcement learning.

- Experience with humanoid or mobile manipulation platforms.

- Experience with machine vision and object detection in robotic applications.

- Knowledge of risk assessment and safety for collaborative applications, including the Machinery Regulation and ISO/TS 15066.

The next chapter of robotics won't be built in a lab. It will be built by people who care about what happens when technology meets the real world.

At TACTILIA, you'll work on one of the hardest open problems in robotics: giving machines the dexterity, reliability and robustness to interact with the physical world at industrial scale.

The technology is taking shape, the team is being built, and the standards around robotic hands and their skills are still open. That means your decisions will have a lasting impact — not just on a product, but on what comes next for Physical AI.

Build the hand. Define the standard. Shape what comes next. 

If you're excited by the challenge of building robotic hands that works reliably in the real world, we'd love to hear from you.

title: Senior Full Stack Engineer
description:
Infisical is looking to hire exceptional talent to join our teams in building the open source security infrastructure stack for the AI era.

We're building a generational company with a world-class team. This isn’t a place to coast — but if you want to grow fast, take ownership, and solve tough problems, you’ll be challenged like nowhere else. 

What We’re Looking For 

We’re looking for an exceptional Senior Full Stack Engineer to help us build, optimize, and expand the foundation of the platform.

We’ve kept our hiring standards exceptionally high since we expect engineers to tackle a broad range of challenges on a day-to-day basis. Examples of past engineering initiatives include developing strategies for secret rotation and dynamic secrets, a gateway to provide secure access to private resources, protocols like EST and KMIP , integrations for syncing secrets across cloud providers, and entire new product lines such as Infisical PKI and Infisical SSH.

You’ll be working closely with our CTO and the rest of the engineering team to:

- Develop and maintain features whilst communicating directly with enterprise customers.

- Expand our newer Infisical PKI , Infisical SSH , and Infisical KMS product lines.

- Experiment with novel approaches for applying AI to secrets management and more broadly security infrastructure.

Requirements 

- Deep technical mastery of the JavaScript ecosystem, particularly React.js, Node.js, and TypeScript (3+).

- Exceptional attention to detail and eager to learn.

- A bias toward action—able to make decisions with incomplete information, iterate quickly, and take calculated risks.

- Based in North or South America.

Bonus 

- Expertise in Go.

- Has some understanding of devops/developer tools.

- Previous founder or startup experience.

- Previous experience building in open source or developer tools in either a professional or personal setting.

- Excellent written and oral communication skills to interact with customers directly.

How You’ll Grow 

In this role, you’ll play a pivotal part in shaping Infisical’s future—making key technical decisions, establishing foundational processes, and tackling complex scalability challenges. As you gain experience and the team expands, you'll have the opportunity to take full ownership of specific areas of our platform, driving them end-to-end with autonomy and impact.

Overall, you’ll be one of the defining pieces of our team as we scale to thousands of customers over the next 18 months.

Team, Values & Benefits 

Our team brings experience from companies like Figma, AWS, and Red Hat. We operate primarily as a remote team but maintain a strong presence in San Francisco, where we have an office. We also get together in person throughout the year for off-sites, conferences, and team gatherings. 

At Infisical, we offer competitive compensation, including both salary and equity options. Additional benefits, such as a lunch stipend and a work setup budget, are available with more details to be found on our careers page .

About Us 

Infisical is the open source security infrastructure platform that engineers use for secrets, certificates, and privileged access management. We help developers and organizations securely manage over 1.5 billion secrets each month including application configuration, database credentials, certificates, and more.

We’ve raised $19M from Y Combinator, Google, and Elad Gil, and our customers include Hugging Face, Lucid, and LG.

Join us on a mission to make security easier for all developers — starting with secrets management.

Deine Rolle bei June Als Tech Lead Grower Marketplace Experience (m/w/d) verantwortest du die technische Entwicklung unseres Marketplace und der dazugehörigen Services. Du berichtest direkt an unsere CTO Anna. 

Du baust einen neuen Engineering Squad von Grund auf auf und übernimmst die technische und fachliche Verantwortung für einen der kommerziell wichtigsten Bereiche von June. Es geht nicht nur darum, gute Software zu bauen: Du setzt technische Richtung, triffst Entscheidungen unter Unsicherheit, entwickelst Menschen, und prägst die Kultur deines Squads. Du sorgst gemeinsam mit dem Produkt-Team dafür, dass wir Funktionen entwickeln, die für unsere Kunden messbaren Mehrwert schaffen. 

Wir geben dir den Kontext und den Freiraum, den du brauchst, um deinen Bereich eigenständig zu führen. Im Gegenzug erwarten wir, dass du Verantwortung übernimmst, Entscheidungen triffst und auch für ihre Konsequenzen einstehst – in einem dynamischen Umfeld, in dem sich Prioritäten verändern und Informationen nicht immer vollständig vorliegen. 

Du bist kein klassischer People Manager. Du führst über technische Tiefe, Klarheit, Entscheidungen und Vertrauen. Du bleibst hands-on im Code, ohne zum technischen Bottleneck zu werden, triffst Architekturentscheidungen und unterstützt dein Team dabei, gemeinsam hochwertige Software zu entwickeln. 

Unser Marketplace basiert auf dem Spryker Commerce OS . Du entwickelst ein klares Verständnis dafür, wann wir innerhalb der Spryker-Konventionen arbeiten, wann wir erweitern und wann eine individuelle Lösung sinnvoll ist. Dabei behältst du immer die langfristige Wartbarkeit und Erweiterbarkeit unserer Plattform im Blick. 

Anforderungen Was du mitbringst - Du hast mehrjährige Erfahrung als Tech Lead oder Senior Engineer in Web- und E-Commerce-Anwendungen sowie fundierte praktische Erfahrung mit PHP und Spryker Commerce OS und weißt, wann du innerhalb der Spryker-Konventionen arbeitest, erweiterst oder bewusst davon abweichst. 

- Du bringst Erfahrung mit API- bzw. Spec-first-Entwicklung sowie mit AWS-Cloud-Infrastrukturen, modernen Deployment-Prozessen und Monitoring mit. 

- Du hast bereits Erfahrung im Teamaufbau und weißt, worauf es ankommt. 

- Du hast Verständnis, Interesse und Lust an Produktentwicklung (Software) und Teamentwicklung (Menschen). 

- Du arbeitest eigenverantwortlich, kommunizierst klar, hast hohe Qualitätsansprüche und sprichst fließend Deutsch sowie sehr gutes Englisch. 

Das wäre ein Plus - Gute Kenntnisse in TypeScript. 

- Erfahrung mit ERP-, Warehouse- oder Commerce-Systemen. 

- Erfahrung mit komplexen Order-, Pricing- oder Inventory/Catalogue-Prozessen. 

- Erfahrung in einem Startup oder schnell wachsenden Technologieunternehmen. 

Aufgabenbereich Was du bei uns bewegst - Du verantwortest Architektur, technische Qualität und Weiterentwicklung des Marketplace und seiner Services. 

- Du baust dein Squad auf, entwickelst deine Teammitglieder weiter und schaffst eine Kultur aus Ownership, Pragmatismus und kontinuierlichem Lernen. 

- Du entwickelst eine klare technische Strategie für den Produktbereich Marketplace Experience und triffst bewusste Entscheidungen darüber, wie wir Spryker einsetzen und erweitern. 

- Du arbeitest eng mit dem Produkt-Team zusammen und übersetzt die Bedürfnisse unserer Käufer und Verkäufer in nachhaltige technische Lösungen.. 

- Du sorgst dafür, dass dein Team Software kontinuierlich, sicher und zuverlässig ausliefert – von der technischen Spezifikation und Architektur über API-Design und Entwicklung bis hin zu Betrieb, Incident Management und kontinuierlicher Verbesserung. 

- Du übernimmst Verantwortung für Performance, Stabilität, Security und Compliance und stellst sicher, dass technische Risiken früh erkannt, bewertet und bewusst adressiert werden. 

- Du nutzt AI selbstverständlich im Engineering-Alltag und hilfst deinem Team dabei, AI sinnvoll und verantwortungsvoll für Entwicklung, Testing, Dokumentation und Code Reviews einzusetzen. 

So arbeiten wir Unsere Teams verantworten ihren Produktbereich komplett: Architektur, API-Design, Entwicklung, Betrieb, Incidents, Security, Compliance. Die kommerziellen KPIs gehören dazu. 

Wir reden mit Kunden, fahren zu ihnen raus, testen unsere Lösungen dort im Betrieb. Verantwortung endet nicht am Merge-Button. 

Die Perspektive Was dich erwartet - Du baust etwas auf, statt ein bestehendes Team zu verwalten. 

- Du bekommst einen klar abgegrenzten Verantwortungsbereich und die Freiheit, ihn zu gestalten. 

- Du arbeitest direkt mit CTO und Product Manager und kannst technische, produktbezogene, kulturprägende und kommerzielle Entscheidungen tatsächlich beeinflussen. 

- Du siehst die Konsequenzen deiner Entscheidungen unmittelbar – im Produkt, im Team und im Geschäft. 

- Hybrides Arbeiten in unserem Büro in Köln sowie regelmäßige Besuche bei Kund*innen, Gärtner*innen und Partner*innen vor Ort 

Diese Stellenbeschreibung ist bewusst meinungsstark und setzt hohe Standards. Wir suchen nicht den perfekten Lebenslauf, sondern Menschen, die bei Connected Growers glücklich werden. Wenn du nicht alle formalen Kriterien erfüllst, dich aber in der Art, wie wir arbeiten und führen, wiedererkennst, freuen wir uns trotzdem über deine Bewerbung. Was dir an einzelnen Punkten noch fehlt, können wir gemeinsam entwickeln – entscheidend ist, dass du das Mindset und die Bereitschaft mitbringst, in diese Rolle hineinzuwachsen. 

Hinweis: Die Stelle wird zunächst über BridgeMaker besetzt und im weiteren Verlauf zu Connected Growers überführt.

title: AI Senior Engineer (Graph)
description:
Back in 2012, we were a group of engineers and designers who decided we wanted to build things—so we did. Able started as an engineering and product hub building for a portfolio of early-stage startups. We built many relationships while developing products that were thoughtful, effective, and genuinely useful. But, since then, we’ve grown… and so has our ambition. 

Now, we’re entering our next chapter—defined by applied AI. AI is a powerful force in the end-to-end software development cycle, and we’re creating practices that allow us to deliver software fast and more effectively than traditional approaches, creating meaningful value for our partners. Today, our builder mindset is driving us to become an AI-native organization across every function. We’re still evolving, and that’s part of the opportunity. If you want to build, learn, and tackle challenges alongside an ambitious team, let’s build together.

This position is 100% remote within LatAm. 

What you’ll be doing 

We are seeking someone who views the Knowledge Graph not just as a database, but as a living organism that requires constant care, feeding, and pruning. You understand that a RAG system is only as good as the data underlying it. You are intrigued by the complexity of ingesting massive, messy datasets and transforming them into clean, connected knowledge.

In short, someone who likes:

- Architecting Graph ETL: Designing and developing robust ETL pipelines specifically for graph ingestion. You aren't just dumping rows into tables; you are determining how disparate data sources connect, evolve, and relate in a graph structure.

- Data Ingestion at Scale: Managing high-volume data streams using tools like Kafka and implementing CDC (Change Data Capture) patterns to ensure the graph reflects real-time reality.

- Automated Graph Hygiene: Writing scripts and jobs for deduplication , orphan node detection , and data consistency checks. You take pride in a clean schema.

- Modeling Time: Handling complex temporal relationships (e.g., how property ownership or financial status changes over time) within the graph.

- Performance Tuning: Ensuring that as the graph grows (25k+ reports and beyond), the underlying query performance remains snappy through optimizing indexes and storage.

What we’re looking for 

We want to work with people who have a passion for collaborating with their teams, building software while nurturing inclusive and respectful relationships with their coworkers. With the ones that are open about their shortcomings and what they do not know now, but remain eager to keep on growing and closing those gaps.

Ideally, they would also have:

- Neo4j Expertise (Must Have): 4+ years of hands-on experience. You master Cypher , schema design, and the operational side of managing a production graph.

- ETL & Pipeline Mastery: Strong background in building data pipelines. You know how to take raw data, clean it, and structure it for graph ingestion.

- Streaming & CDC: Familiarity with event streaming platforms like Kafka and Change Data Capture methodologies to sync operational databases with the graph.

- Python Proficiency: Strong Python skills for writing ingestion scripts, maintenance jobs, and custom graph algorithms.

- Data Integrity Focus: Experience implementing automated jobs for entity resolution , deduplication, and quality assurance.

Nice-to-Have: 

- C# Knowledge: Ability to read or contribute to C# codebases.

- Domain Experience: Prior work in Finance or Real Estate sectors.

Able is powered by curious, thoughtful people who care about what they build and how they build it. We’re actively investing in our team through AI training, knowledge-sharing, and hands-on experimentation to ensure everyone grows alongside the technology.

This position is 100% remote within LatAm. Strong verbal and written communication skills in English are a requirement. As a team member, you can expect:

- To work 40 hours per week, and be available during normal business hours as needed.

- Payments made in USD.

- 18 days of PTO per year, observance of local holidays, and an annual break between Christmas and New Years.

- Wellness + Remote Stipend

- AI Voucher

About Able 

Able builds technology products in a portfolio model. We believe that people, teams, and processes are more important than the ideas themselves, so we’ve focused on bringing great people together, and investing in their growth.

We’ve built products in a variety of industries. Everything from media to finance to toys to healthcare. Sometimes we work with management teams to help their businesses grow faster or unlock value using technology. Other times we start or buy businesses outright. Each time, we look for opportunities to leverage technology built at the portfolio-level to drive value faster.

Able is committed to inclusion and diversity and is an equal-opportunity employer. All applicants will receive consideration without regard to race, color, religion, gender, gender identity, sexual orientation, national origin, disability, or veteran status.

This is but the beginning of a conversation we’d love to have with you.

Apply, and let’s get this adventure started!

- Build and maintain the roadmap: reconcile project timelines, our concept of operations and component readiness into one roadmap that is used to set priorities, not to describe them afterwards.

- A diverse and vibrant international environment of 30+ different nationalities

You will create and own the AI architecture and best practices the rest of the company utilizes. You will also own the initiatives that put agents into production. You should know how to build and fine-tune foundation models from the ground up, how to engineer best-in-class harnesses, and how to create best practices for agentic engineering that engineering teams adopt to 10x their productivity—without sacrificing quality. Your mindset will be that of a builder and an architect, someone who solves problems in the system itself. No problem will be too large or too small for you to solve yourself. You will set the technical direction and hold the cadenced meetings that turns technical strategy into working, production-ready outcomes. You will be in the design reviews and in the code, not adjacent to them. You will move fast, and you will ensure our engineering team is never the reason an initiative slows down.

You are the technical owner of all Toptal’s products. You will collaborate closely with Product to design infrastructure that exposes Toptal’s core business logic through modular interfaces the rest of the business can build on. Alongside a group of hands-on executives, your engineering discipline directly shapes Toptal’s growth, profitability, and operational excellence.

You will own resourcing and workforce planning as a doer: scoping the work, sizing the teams, planning headcount against it, defining the role and the bar for every seat. None of that is beneath the role, and we are not interested in someone who thinks these tasks can be done properly by handing it off to HR. Hiring is the highest-leverage work you do, and we want someone who is visibly excited about hiring A-players—with a sense of urgency.

Then, you lead the team. You will set the standards, develop people against those standards, and know exactly who is meeting those standards.

You will be one of Toptal’s foremost experts on AI, and you will stay ahead of a field that never stops moving. You will coach engineers on agentic best practices, show the executive team what is newly possible with the new AI tooling, and push AI into every function at Toptal.

This role runs on high-energy execution and attention to detail. You will bring urgency to every part of it and measure yourself on outcomes. We are not looking for someone to oversee this work. We are looking for someone to drive it and get into the detiwls.

This is a remote position. Resumes and communication must be submitted in English.

Responsibilities:

The following information is intended to describe the general nature and level of work being performed. It is not intended to be an exhaustive list of all duties, responsibilities, or required skills. 

One precondition runs through all of it: you conceive the strategy. You will form your own view of where engineering and AI should go, build the case, and bring the CEO a strategy to react to, not a request for direction.

AI and agentic engineering 

- Own Toptal’s AI technology strategy and the architecture beneath it: model selection and fine-tuning, harness design, orchestration, retrieval, context engineering, tool and MCP integration, guardrails, evaluation, and cost control, exposed as primitives every team composes against.

- Deploy agentic engineering at scale against the work that runs this business: matching, vetting, onboarding, delivery, and internal operations. Own the outcomes those agents are accountable for.

- Make AI quality measurable. Own the evals, the regression suites, and the review loops, so quality here is proven rather than claimed.

- Rebuild how the platform gets built and operated, raising output per engineer through AI-assisted development, review, testing, and operations. Engineers have to want this, not comply with it, and creating that pull is on you.

Team, resourcing, and accountability 

- Decide what a team should look like now that the roles have blurred, where the product manager believes they can design and code, the engineer believes they can do product and design, and the designer believes they can code and do product.

- Own resourcing and workforce planning: scope the roadmap into buildable work, plan headcount and sequence, write the specs, and hit time-sensitive hiring commitments.

- Own the bar for the team: assess talent honestly, develop people against the bar, and hold it as the organization grows.

Platform and execution 

- Own the architecture end to end, from services and data flows to interfaces and system boundaries, and hold the standards that keep it coherent as it grows.

- Own throughput, reliability, and the platform layer beneath them, including the AI-dependent paths where latency, drift, and provider outages are real failure modes. Own build-versus-buy, technical debt, secure-by-design architecture, responsible AI, and the engineering and AI cost structure down to inference and token spend.

In the first week, expect to:

- Learn Toptal’s model and platform architecture, and meet the leaders you will depend on across Engineering, Product, Industries, and Services.

- Establish a direct, working rhythm with the CEO.

In the first month, expect to:

- Assess the engineering function honestly, and assess AI maturity with it: what is really in production, what is measured, what is duplicated, and what should be shut down.

- Assess the team against the bar this role requires, and bring the executive team a strategy no one asked you for.

In the first three months, expect to:

- Be executing your own plan, with a review cadence and clear accountability at every level, and your resourcing plan presented.

- Stand up the shared AI architecture and evals, and put one agentic workflow into production with a baseline and a measured result.

In the first six months, expect to:

- Show business impact from agents in production in at least two core workflows, with the evidence behind it.

- Have the leadership team you need, with the bar visibly raised, and throughput and reliability moving on the paths that matter most.

In the first year, expect to:

- Run an engineering organization recognized inside and outside Toptal as one of the most advanced in the industry, with the pull on AI now coming from engineering.

- Have AI leverage embedded in the architecture and the operating model, not living in a portfolio of pilots, and the team you built delivering against plan.

Qualifications and Job Requirements:

- Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Engineering, or a related technical field is required, and an advanced degree is strongly preferred.

- 15+ years of progressive engineering leadership, including significant time as a CTO or VP of Engineering, or as a direct report to one at meaningful scale.

- Deep, current, hands-on command of modern AI engineering: foundation models, agentic architectures, harness design, retrieval, context engineering, fine-tuning, and evaluation. You have shipped and operated these in production, and you know how to build and fine-tune foundation models from the ground up.

- Agentic systems deployed at scale against real business processes, with measured outcomes on cost, cycle time, quality, or revenue, and a record of retiring what did not work.

- Rigor about evaluation. You can explain precisely how you knew a model, prompt, or agent change was an improvement, and you can show the evidence.

- Command of the economics underneath it: model routing, hosted versus self-hosted, inference capacity, latency and cost budgets, and staying portable across providers.

- Further ahead on AI than the executives around you, able to teach it, and proven at moving an organization to adopt something it was not asking for.

- You create strategy rather than administer it, and you win arguments on evidence rather than authority, including your view on what a team should look like in the age of AI.

- Proven ownership of resourcing and workforce planning, and a hiring track record you can quantify. You have made the hard calls when someone was not clearing the bar.

- Currently hands-on. You read and write code, you can take apart a design document or an eval harness and find the flaw in it, and you command distributed systems, service architecture, data-intensive applications, and cloud infrastructure at scale.

- Experience scaling and modernizing a large existing codebase without stopping the business. You have replaced load-bearing systems in flight, not only built greenfield.

- Experience leading a globally distributed, remote team at a technology or hyper-growth company is required. A high-volume, two-sided marketplace or multi-tenant platform is a significant plus.

- Outstanding written and verbal communication skills.

- Speed, ownership, and quality. You move with urgency, decide without perfect information, and treat everything you deliver as a reflection of yourself.

- You must be a world-class individual contributor to thrive at Toptal. You will not be here just to tell other people what to do.

title: Staff Backend Engineer, Commerce
description:
AI at Zapier 

At Zapier , we build and use automation every day to make work more efficient, creative, and human. So if you’re using AI tools while applying here - that’s great! We just ask that you use them responsibly and transparently .

Check out our guidance on How to Collaborate with AI During Zapier’s Hiring Process , including how to use AI tools like ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, or others during our hiring process - and when not to.

Job Posted: April 29, 2026

Updated: June 19, 2026

Location: Americas - North, Central and South America, EMEA, APAC

Hi there!

Zapier's mission is to make automation work for everyone. That mission is funded by revenue — and every dollar of it flows through our Commerce Zone. We build and operate the infrastructure behind billing, subscriptions, payments, pricing, entitlements, and checkout across everything Zapier ships: self-serve plans, enterprise contracts, and ecosystem offerings. When a customer upgrades, renews, changes plans, or pays an invoice, our systems make it happen — correctly, instantly, and at scale.

We're hiring a Staff Engineer to own the technical vision and long-term architecture for the Commerce Zone. You'll define the pricing primitives, service boundaries, and data models that let Zapier ship pricing and packaging changes in days instead of months — while keeping every dollar accounted for accurately. That means designing the framework and abstractions product teams plug into so they can launch new SKUs without becoming billing experts, building configuration-driven infrastructure for pricing experimentation, and ensuring the platform evolves without foundational rewrites.

This is production-critical, finance-grade infrastructure where correctness is non-negotiable. You'll drive alignment across teams in a space defined by high ambiguity and competing constraints, working closely with Product, Engineering, Finance, and Sales. The role is particularly exciting because decisions here ripple across Zapier — shaping how the company monetizes its next phase of growth.

- 
Our Commitment to Applicants 

- 
Culture and Values at Zapier 

- 
Zapier Guide to Remote Work 

- 
Zapier Code of Conduct 

- 
Diversity and Inclusivity at Zapier 

About You 

- 
Proven engineering impact: You've driven outcomes in complex, production systems at scale — shipping projects that delivered measurable improvements in environments where requirements shifted under you. You separate essential from accidental complexity, make tradeoffs explicit, and use data to inform decisions without becoming paralyzed by it. Many strong candidates have 8+ years of experience, but we hire for impact and capability, not tenure.

- 
Billing/payments/monetization domain experience: You bring strong domain knowledge in billing systems, subscription management, payment processing, or financial platforms. You understand metered billing, pricing models, entitlements, revenue recognition, and the operational complexity of supporting enterprise customers. You know that billing isn't just a backend problem — it touches sales, finance, support, and product, and you've navigated that reality.

- 
API, platform, and performance expertise: You've designed and built APIs that serve multiple consumers — internal teams, external partners, and user-facing products — and you know how to evolve systems without breaking existing integrations. You have a track record of identifying and resolving performance bottlenecks through profiling, caching, database optimization, and delivering measurable improvements that impact user experience and conversion.

- 
Outcome-driven and customer-focused: You care deeply about the problems our customers are trying to solve and define success by the results they achieve — not the elegance of the technical solution. You fall in love with the problem, not your first implementation, and are willing to rethink or pivot when it better serves the customer and the business.

- 
Cross-team leadership and proactive ownership: You've led technical initiatives that span multiple teams and operate with end-to-end ownership. You gather requirements, surface risks early, align stakeholders, and drive ambiguous problems through to measurable outcomes. You're a trusted partner to Engineering, Product, and Design leadership — helping shape roadmaps, translating business strategy into technical direction, and amplifying other engineers by raising standards and building durable foundations that create leverage across teams.

- 
AI fluency: You use AI coding tools as a regular part of your workflow and have a point of view on where they accelerate delivery and where human judgment is non-negotiable. In a high-correctness domain like payments and billing, you know the difference between automating boilerplate and trusting AI with revenue logic — and you bring that judgment to the engineers you work with.

- 
Comfort with complexity: You're at home in large, mature codebases — you know how to navigate a monolith, find the right leverage points, and make meaningful progress without waiting for a clean slate.

Things You’ll Do 

- 
Serve as a technical leader within the Commerce Zone: You’ll operate as part of the zone’s leadership team, partnering closely with Engineering, Product, and Design to shape strategy and roadmap decisions. You’ll translate business context into technical direction—and ensure engineering tradeoffs are clearly understood at the business level.

- 
Shape the long-term platform vision: You’ll define and evolve the architectural direction of the Commerce Zone, balancing near-term delivery with long-term durability, extensibility, and operational excellence.

- 
Lead high-impact technical initiatives: You’ll drive the strategic evolution of our monetization platform—decoupling billing from account systems, clarifying system boundaries, and consolidating pricing infrastructure. You’ll build flexible, configurable foundations that enable fast Pricing and Packaging experimentation and seamless launch moments across the customer lifecycle, while supporting clean, reliable data for Finance and Pricing & Packaging.

- 
Own and strengthen revenue-critical systems: You’ll be responsible for systems across the Commerce Zone—Billing, Pricing, Payments, Checkout, and Entitlements—ensuring they are resilient, observable, and correct. You’ll raise the bar on proactive detection, safe rollback mechanisms, and revenue accuracy—catching issues before customers do. You’ll systematically reduce structural and technical debt, eliminate recurring operational pain points, and strengthen architectural foundations to prevent revenue-impacting incidents before they emerge.

- 
Guide high-impact technical decisions: You’ll influence API design, data modeling, caching strategies, and system architecture—optimizing for scalability, developer experience, and rapid pricing and packaging iteration.

- 
Partner deeply across Zapier: You’ll collaborate closely with Pricing & Packaging, Product, and Design teams to drive ARR growth and craft seamless, intuitive, and lovable monetization journeys for self-serve, enterprise, and ecosystem customers. You’ll also work with Support and Operations to ensure robust admin tooling and exceptional customer experiences across upgrades, billing changes, and subscription management.

- 
Drive measurable improvements: You’ll identify performance bottlenecks and deliver optimizations that show up in the metrics—reduced latency, improved reliability, stronger customer experiences, and improved conversion and retention.

- 
Mentor engineers and raise the technical bar: You’ll share patterns and tooling, conduct thoughtful code reviews, and grow engineering capability across the zone. You’ll be a go-to resource for engineers tackling complex monetization and platform challenges.

- 
Champion documentation and developer experience: You’ll ensure our systems are well-documented and easy to adopt, reducing friction and accelerating development across the organization.

How to Apply 

At Zapier, we believe that diverse perspectives and experiences make us better, which is why we have a non-standard application process designed to promote inclusion and equity. We're looking for the best fit for each of our roles, regardless of the type of companies in your background, so we encourage you to apply even if your skills and experiences don’t exactly match the job description. All we ask is that you answer a few in-depth questions in our application that would typically be asked at the start of an interview process. This helps speed things up by letting us get to know you and your skillset a bit better right out of the gate. Please be sure to answer each question; the resume and CV fields are optional.

Education is not a requirement for our roles; however, if you receive an offer, you will need to include your most recent educational experience as part of our background check process.

After you apply, you are going to hear back from us—even if we don’t see an immediate fit with our team. In fact, throughout the process, we strive to never go more than seven days without letting you know the status of your application. We know we’ll make mistakes from time to time, so if you ever have questions about where you stand or about the process, just ask your recruiter!

Zapier is an equal-opportunity employer and we're excited to work with talented and empathetic people of all identities. Zapier does not discriminate based on someone's identity in any aspect of hiring or employment as required by law and in line with our commitment to Diversity, Inclusion, Belonging and Equity. Our code of conduct provides a beacon for the kind of company we strive to be, and we celebrate our differences because those differences are what allow us to make a product that serves a global user base. Zapier will consider all qualified applicants, including those with criminal histories, consistent with applicable laws.

Zapier prioritizes the security of our customers' information and is dedicated to adhering to all applicable data privacy laws. You can review our privacy policy here .

Zapier is committed to inclusion. As part of this commitment, Zapier welcomes applications from individuals with disabilities and will work to provide reasonable accommodations. If reasonable accommodations are needed to participate in the job application or interview process, please contact jobs@zapier.com .

Application Deadline: 

The anticipated application window is 30 days from the date job is posted, unless the number of applicants requires it to close sooner or later, or if the position is filled.

Even though we’re an all-remote company, we still need to be thoughtful about where we have Zapiens working. Check out this resource for a list of countries where we currently cannot have Zapiens permanently working.
